body.en: When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, eight angles appear — but only two distinct measures. Knowing which pairs are equal and which are supplementary unlocks most angle-chase problems.
Corresponding angles are equal; alternate (interior or exterior) angles are equal; co-interior (same-side interior) angles are supplementary, summing to \( 180^{\circ} \).

Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Lines & Angles)

body.en:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle is \( 72^{\circ} \). Find its alternate interior angle.

Alternate interior angles are equal:

\[ 72^{\circ}. \]

A co-interior angle measures \( 110^{\circ} \). Find the other co-interior angle.

\[ 180^{\circ}-110^{\circ}=70^{\circ}. \]

label.en: Common Pitfall — Conflating Alternate and Consecutive Angles

body.en: A frequent error on SAT and ACT geometry questions is equating consecutive (same-side) interior angles instead of setting their sum to \( 180^{\circ} \). Remember the letter shapes: Z-angles (alternate interior) are equal; F-angles (corresponding) are equal; but C-angles (consecutive interior) are supplementary.

label.en: Worked Example C — Lines & Angles (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): The linear system \( 11u + 24y = 228 \) and \( 22u + (h + 24)y = 463 \) has no solution. Compute the constant parameter \( h \).

Step-by-Step Solution: A linear system has no solution when the lines are parallel and distinct: \( \frac{22}{11} = \frac{h + 24}{24} \implies h = 24 \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Lines & Angles (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): In the \( xy \)-plane, line \( \ell \) passes through \( (0, 9) \) and is perpendicular to \( y = -\frac{1}{20}x + 16 \). Compute the \( y \)-coordinate \( h(14) \) on \( \ell \) at \( u = 14 \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The slope of \( \ell \) is \( m = 20 \), so \( y = 20x + 9 \). At \( x = 14 \), \( y = 20(14) + 9 = 289 \).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Lines & Angles)

rows.en: Reading radius of \((x-3)^2 + (y+7)^2 = 16\) as \(r = 16\) or center as \((-3, 7)\)
Confuses \(r^2\) with \(r\) and forgets to flip the signs inside \((x-h)\) and \((y-k)\).
Take the square root and negate the constants: center \((3, -7)\), radius \(r = \sqrt{16} = 4\).
Using SSA (two sides and a non-included angle) to claim triangle congruence
The ambiguous case of the Sine Rule allows two distinct triangles (\(\theta\) and \(180^\circ - \theta\)).
Use valid congruence criteria only: SSS, SAS (included angle), ASA, AAS, or HL/RHS.
Cubing the area ratio \((A_1/A_2)^3\) to find the volume ratio of similar solids
Area ratio is already \(k^2\), so cubing it gives \(k^6\) instead of \(k^3\).
First take the square root to get linear scale factor \(k = \sqrt{A_1/A_2}\), then cube \(k^3\).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Lines & Angles

body.en: Geometric Auxiliary-Line Strategy (Honors Euclidean & Analytic Geometry): Whenever a circle problem includes a tangent line, draw the radius to the point of tangency and mark \(90^\circ\) immediately; whenever it includes a chord, drop the perpendicular bisector from the center to form a right triangle.

question.en: Two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal line. Two consecutive interior angles have measures \( (3x - 10)^{\circ} \) and \( (2x + 25)^{\circ} \). Find the measure of the acute angle.

solution.en:
Solution: Consecutive interior angles are supplementary, so they sum to \( 180^{\circ} \):

\[ (3x - 10) + (2x + 25) = 180 \implies 5x + 15 = 180 \implies 5x = 165 \implies x = 33. \]

Substitute \( x = 33 \) into both angle expressions:

\[ 3(33) - 10 = 89^{\circ}, \quad 2(33) + 25 = 91^{\circ}. \]

The acute angle has measure \( 89^{\circ} \).

question.en: Two parallel lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) are cut by a transversal \(T\). A pair of alternate exterior angles are given by \((7x - 14)^{\circ}\) and \((4x + 31)^{\circ}\). Find the value of \(x\) and the measure of each alternate exterior angle.

solution.en:
Step 1: Set up the equation using alternate exterior angles: Alternate exterior angles created by parallel lines are congruent:

\[ 7x - 14 = 4x + 31 \implies 3x = 45 \implies x = 15. \]

Step 2: Evaluate the angle measure:

\[ 7(15) - 14 = 105 - 14 = 91^{\circ}. \]

Check: \(4(15) + 31 = 60 + 31 = 91^{\circ}\). Both alternate exterior angles measure \(91^{\circ}\).

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] The linear inequality \( 3u - 18 \le -9 \) restricts the positive integer \( u \) on the number line. Compute the number of positive integers \( u \) in the solution set \( h \).

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Lines & Angles and start from \( 3u - 18 \le -9 \).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \( 18 \).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

solution.en: Adding \( 18 \) and dividing by \( 3 \) gives \( u \le 3 \), which yields \( 3 \) positive integers.
